rules.title: Fitted with relaxed
rules.text: Balance volume: pair a relaxed piece with a fitted one. Wide trousers want a neat top; a slouchy knit wants slim legs.

rules.title: Cropped meets high-rise
rules.text: A cropped top or jacket should meet a high waistband, so no gap breaks the line and the legs look longer.

rules.title: Show the waist with wide legs
rules.text: With wide-leg trousers, tuck or crop the top so the waist shows; volume on volume swamps the frame.

rules.title: The third piece
rules.text: Top and bottom make clothes; a third piece makes an outfit. Add a blazer, cardigan, overshirt or a scarf to finish.

rules.title: Oversized over slim
rules.text: An oversized blazer or knit looks deliberate over slim trousers or leggings, not over equally baggy bottoms.

rules.title: Match jacket length to skirt
rules.text: A cropped blazer suits a skirt with a defined waist; an oversized blazer suits a fuller, longer skirt.

rules.title: Full skirt, slim top
rules.text: Balance a full midi skirt with a slim, fine-knit top and a sleek shoe to keep the shape clean.

rules.title: Lengthen long hems
rules.text: Maxi dresses and long wide-leg trousers look less swamping with a pointed toe or a little height.

rules.title: Blend to lengthen
rules.text: Match an under-layer to your trousers to lengthen the legs, or to your top to lengthen the torso.

rules.title: Mind the trouser break
rules.text: Slim trousers look sharpest with little or no break; a slight break is the most versatile, from loafers to sneakers.

rules.title: Let the hem pick the shoe
rules.text: Puddling wide legs need a heel or chunky sole; cropped hems let flats, sandals and loafers show.

rules.title: Room for layers
rules.text: Outer layers need room for what's beneath but shouldn't be oversized. If it won't button over your layers, it's too small.

rules.title: Jumpsuit length and waist
rules.text: A jumpsuit should reach the ankle and sit in at the waist; add a belt if a loose one swallows your shape.

rules.title: Hoodie under tailoring
rules.text: Under a blazer, keep the hoodie plain and trim, roomy but not sloppy, with sleeves ending at the wrist.

rules.title: Match shoe to formality
rules.text: Match the shoe to the outfit's formality: lace-ups for tailoring, loafers for smart casual, sneakers and sandals for casual.

rules.title: Sneakers with suits, done right
rules.text: Clean, low-profile leather sneakers now sit fine under a suit for smart-casual events. Keep runners and chunky soles out of it.

rules.title: Formal codes stay formal
rules.text: Where an invitation says black tie or business formal, wear proper leather shoes. Sneakers suit relaxed or unstated codes only.

rules.title: White sneakers go furthest
rules.text: White or cream sneakers suit almost any suit colour; black sneakers with a dark suit can look schoolboyish.

rules.title: Shorter shorts, lighter shoes
rules.text: The shorter the shorts, the more casual the shoe: sneakers and sandals for short hems, loafers for knee-length tailored shorts.

rules.title: No heavy shoes with shorts
rules.text: Boots and black dress shoes look heavy with shorts. Choose loafers, espadrilles, sneakers or sandals instead.

rules.title: Loafers like a narrow hem
rules.text: Loafers look best with tapered or cropped legs; a wide opening covers the low vamp and makes feet look stubby.

rules.title: Brown suede for denim
rules.text: Brown suede is the easiest leather with jeans. Sleek black shoes suit black or grey denim better than indigo.

rules.title: Sneakers with dresses
rules.text: Pick the sneaker to suit the dress: slim retro runners for crisp cottons, chunkier pairs for minis and slips.

rules.title: Socks follow trousers
rules.text: Match socks to trousers rather than shoes; when the ankle shows, the leg looks longer and the outfit calmer.

rules.title: When to go no-show
rules.text: No-show socks suit loafers, boat shoes and sneakers with shorts or cropped trousers. Keep them away from dress shoes.

rules.title: Sports socks for sport
rules.text: White athletic socks belong with athletic shoes only.

rules.title: One pattern leads
rules.text: Let one pattern lead and keep the others quiet; a busy pattern beside another busy pattern fights.

rules.title: Vary the scale
rules.text: When mixing two patterns, make one large and one small so each reads clearly.

rules.title: Share a colour
rules.text: Mixed prints should share at least one colour and a similar intensity; a bright print beside a muted one looks accidental.

rules.title: Stripes act as neutrals
rules.text: Fine stripes behave almost like a solid, which makes them the easiest pattern to add to a print.

rules.title: Same pattern twice
rules.text: Stripe on stripe or check on check works only when the scales are clearly different; similar sizes shimmer.

rules.title: Use a solid bridge
rules.text: A solid piece between two patterns calms the mix. When in doubt, add a plain layer.

rules.title: Animal print as a neutral
rules.text: Animal print can act as a neutral with solids and stripes; pair it with one other print at most.

rules.title: Contrast your textures
rules.text: Pair opposites: smooth with rough, matte with shine. Silk with knit, or leather with wool, adds depth to a plain palette.

rules.title: Texture rescues tonal outfits
rules.text: In a one-colour or neutral outfit, vary fabrics and weaves so the look doesn't fall flat.

rules.title: Keep a shared colour story
rules.text: Textured pieces work best in a shared colour family, so the texture reads rather than the clash.

rules.title: Fabric follows the season
rules.text: Linen, seersucker and light cotton for summer; tweed, flannel, corduroy and heavier wool for winter.

rules.title: Match knit to shirt weight
rules.text: Pair fine-gauge knits with crisp, smooth shirts, and chunkier knits with sturdier oxford, denim or flannel.

rules.title: Thin to thick
rules.text: Layer from thin to thick: the lightest fabric next to the body, the heaviest on the outside.

rules.title: Three visible layers
rules.text: Three visible layers is the sweet spot; a fourth usually tips into bulk. An undershirt doesn't count.

rules.title: Every layer stands alone
rules.text: Each layer should look good on its own, so the outfit still works when the coat comes off.

rules.title: Light inside, dark outside
rules.text: Lighter colours inside and darker ones outside is a reliable starting point, not a fixed law.

rules.title: Shirt cuff and collar under knits
rules.text: Under a jumper, let a few millimetres of shirt cuff show and keep the collar points inside the neckline.

rules.title: Layering a slip dress
rules.text: Wear a fine tee or thin knit under a slip dress, and a blazer or leather jacket over it for structure.

rules.title: Gilet for smart warmth
rules.text: A slim padded gilet fits under a blazer or coat for warmth without bulky sleeves.

rules.title: Hoodies under tailoring
rules.text: A plain hoodie under a blazer or overcoat is now an accepted high-low look for relaxed offices and weekends.

rules.title: Hem shape decides
rules.text: Straight hems are made to be worn out; long curved tails are made to be tucked.

rules.title: Untucked length
rules.text: Worn untucked, a shirt should end around mid-fly. Any longer and it needs tucking.

rules.title: Tuck under tailoring
rules.text: Tuck any shirt worn under a blazer or waistcoat. Under a jumper, tuck for smart looks; with jeans, an inch of tail can show.

rules.title: The front tuck
rules.text: A front or French tuck defines the waist of a loose tee or knit without a full tuck's formality; it suits mid to high rises.

rules.title: Occasion beats hem
rules.text: When the hem and the occasion disagree, the occasion wins: tuck for weddings, interviews and smart dinners.

rules.title: Polos by bottom
rules.text: Tuck a polo into tailored trousers or chinos; with jeans or shorts, wear it out or half-tucked.

rules.title: Contrast your washes
rules.text: For double denim, keep washes a couple of shades apart, usually darker on the bottom.

rules.title: Or commit to one wash
rules.text: A fully matching wash reads as a deliberate set; a near-miss looks accidental.

rules.title: Break up the blue
rules.text: A white tee or striped knit between two denim pieces stops double denim looking heavy.

rules.title: Vary the fit
rules.text: In double denim, vary the fits: relaxed jeans with a neat jacket, slim jeans with a boxy one.

rules.title: Jeans under a blazer
rules.text: With a blazer, choose dark, clean, straight jeans with no rips, and keep them darker than the jacket.

rules.title: Belt matches shoes
rules.text: Keep belt and shoes in the same colour family and finish: brown with brown, suede with suede.

rules.title: Don't mix black and brown
rules.text: Avoid mixing black and brown leathers in one outfit unless it is clearly intentional.

rules.title: Match your hardware
rules.text: Match the belt buckle to your watch and other hardware: silver with silver, gold with gold.

rules.title: Mixed metals in jewellery
rules.text: Mixing gold and silver jewellery is now accepted; it looks intended when the pieces are stacked or layered together.

rules.title: Casual relaxes the rules
rules.text: Leather and metal matching matters most with tailoring. With sneakers and casual clothes, a canvas or braided belt is fine.

rules.title: Belt width
rules.text: A dress belt about 3 cm wide suits tailoring; wider, chunkier belts belong with jeans.

rules.title: The knit tie
rules.text: A knit tie is the casual tie: wear it with oxford shirts, tweed or cotton jackets and dark jeans, not sleek business suits.

rules.title: Ties and jumpers
rules.text: A tie works under a V-neck or open cardigan; under a crew neck the knot disappears.

rules.title: Backpacks and suits
rules.text: Backpacks suit blazer-and-jeans looks. With a full suit, carry a structured bag so straps don't crush the shoulders.

rules.title: High-low done right
rules.text: High-low works when one piece breaks the formality and the rest stays sharp: clean sneakers, a pressed tee, a well-cut suit.

rules.title: A suit jacket is not a blazer
rules.text: A smooth suit jacket worn alone with jeans looks like half a suit; choose a textured jacket instead.

rules.title: Coats for tailoring
rules.text: Over tailoring, a wool overcoat, topcoat or trench is the classic choice; parkas and puffers dress a suit down.

rules.title: Puffers with suits
rules.text: If a puffer must go with tailoring, choose a slim, dark, hoodless one, or wear a gilet under the jacket.

rules.title: Cargo has a ceiling
rules.text: Cargo trousers can look smart but never formal; skip dress shirts, ties and sleek dress shoes with them.

rules.title: Evening means evening shoes
rules.text: Evening dress calls for evening shoes, such as heels, and a small evening bag like a clutch. Trainers and flip-flops break the code.
